$comment: Arm A prompt set, issue 105. EXTRACTED from docs/research/activation-protocol.md, never authored here: the protocol prose stays authoritative for what each prompt is for and why the control group is read-only, and conformance/benchmark.py asserts every string below still appears there verbatim. Two files holding twenty prompts is a drift hazard, and the check is what makes it survivable -- edit the protocol, not this file, and re-extract. WHY BATCHING IS SAFE HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE: the protocol's first rule is one prompt per session, because once prompt 1 activates governance every later prompt in that chat measures persistence instead. A runner does not break that rule, it enforces it -- prepare() gives every prompt a fresh copy of the target and a fresh process, so twenty runs are twenty sessions. The thing a human must not do by hand is exactly the thing a loop does correctly. ARM A ONLY: prepare() strips .repo-governor.json, so every run here is un-onboarded by construction. Arm B needs a bound target and this file cannot express it.
